snippets.title: Arrakis Security emerges from stealth to secure the AI workforce | Israel Defense
snippets.snippet: # Arrakis Security emerges from stealth to secure the AI workforce Israeli cybersecurity startup Arrakis Security has emerged from stealth with an $8 million seed round and a platform designed to secure the rise of autonomous AI agents inside enterprises. “AI agents have become the new digital workforce,” wrote Tal Baron, co-founder and CEO of Arrakis, in a blog post announcing the company’s launch. ... The $8 million seed round was led by Hetz Ventures, with backing from cybersecurity and AI executives including Mati Staniszewski, CEO of ElevenLabs; Ofer Smadari, CEO of Torq; Amitai Ratzon, CEO of Pentera; and senior executives from Palantir. According to Hetz Ventures General Partner Pavel Livshiz, the security layer around AI agents is still in its early stages, and enterprises need ways to govern these systems without slowing AI adoption. With the new funding, Arrakis plans to expand its R&D team in Israel as companies move from experimenting with AI assistants to deploying autonomous systems across business operations.
